body:
Picked up as the lowest-numbered genuinely actionable open item after confirming SECTIONS 1-138
are either fully closed or blocked on human action (API keys/credit balance/sudo/physical
device/founder product decisions - cross-checked against HUMAN UNBLOCK QUEUE, all consistent).
Web research only, no purchases or vendor commitments made - matches S135-02's established
pattern (research done by Claude Code, final vendor SELECTION left as a founder call).

TIER 1 - STINKIES COMMISSAIRE ($9, polypropylene handle, nylon bristle, 500-unit MOQ target):
Well-served market. Multiple real OEM/ODM manufacturers found with MOQ in the 500-1000 range,
matching the brief exactly:
- Changzhou Freshday Household Products - manual toothbrush OEM/ODM, explicitly offers DuPont
  Tynex bristle option (matches brief's bristle spec even though only ULTRA's brief names Tynex
  by name; worth requesting for COMMISSAIRE too as a possible quality upgrade at similar cost).
- Relish Tech - BSCI/ISO certified, quotes MOQ as low as 50 units on premium stock designs
  (well under the brief's 500-unit target, gives room for a smaller pilot batch before full commit).
- puretoothbrushes.com - DuPont-bristle option explicitly offered on customized OEM-logo line.
Real gap, same class as S135-02's: exact per-500-unit landed cost is not extractable via static
search - all of these gate real pricing behind a quote-request/RFQ form, not a public calculator.
Direct RFQ to 2-3 of the above is the real next step before a PO.

TIER 2 - ULTRA ($68, solid brass cold-forged handle w/ PVD matte black + diamond knurl, DuPont
Tynex head, 250-unit MOQ target):
Real finding, more consequential than the brief assumed: no manufacturer sells an integrated
"brass toothbrush" as a catalog product. This tier requires a two-vendor supply chain, not one:
  (a) HANDLE - brass CNC-turning + knurl + PVD-black shops exist and are a strong match:
      edcpart.com (small-batch EDC/pen CNC machining, brass + titanium, PVD black, MOQ from
      1 piece up through 500-unit runs) and 3qmachining.com (OEM EDC gear machining, brass,
      explicit "PVD Coating in Black/Gold/Rainbow", stated NO MOQ). Both are drawn from the
      EDC-pen/knife industry, not oral care - but the machining spec (cold-forged/CNC brass,
      diamond knurl mid-section, PVD matte black, precision engraving) is their exact bread and
      butter, and their MOQ floors are far more forgiving than the brief assumed (down to 1 unit
      for prototyping vs. the 250-unit target).
  (b) HEAD - no off-the-shelf "press-fit replaceable head, 15mm OD neck" product exists anywhere
      found. This is new tooling, not a catalog pick: a Tynex-capable toothbrush-head OEM (same
      family as Tier 1's candidates) would need to design and mold a custom head to mate with
      whichever handle vendor's neck spec - a real tooling/mold fee applies, amount unknown until
      RFQ'd directly.
  (c) ASSEMBLY - neither vendor family does both halves; a third step (in-house fit-check + QC,
      or a 3PL assembly pass) is needed to mate handle to head before this is a sellable unit.
Bottom line: ULTRA is buildable but is a 3-vendor/3-step supply chain assembled for the first
time for this product, not a single vendor pick like the brief's Production Schedule table implies.
This is worth surfacing to the founder as part of the eventual vendor-selection decision, not
just "which vendor" but "confirm the 3-step handle/head/assembly shape before committing."

Not decided here (same as S135-02): actual vendor selection for either tier is a founder call,
not Claude Code's to make - HUMAN UNBLOCK QUEUE row added.

⚓ ☃
title: S139-02: toothbrush manufacturing vendor research (STINKIES COMMISSAIRE + ULTRA)
